They are the source of truth after generation; regenerate = rerun/edit script. No sheet exists for 26.x. They cover attributes, sounds, etc.; the only texture/resource-pack related line is `setItemModel(NamespacedKey)` and datacomponent mention (sheets/1.21.11.md:61).
- **Rules**: `rules/failure-rules.json` (12 KB; 18 rules: 12 for `*`, 3 for 1.21.4-1.21.11, 1 for 1.21.1, 1 for 1.21.11, 1 for 1.21.8-1.21.11); mined with `tools/mine-rules.py`. Injected as "LESSONS FROM EARLIER FAILED BUILDS".
- Note: `GameSupport.knowledge` / `KnowledgePack` (lib/cyrus/games/support.ts:55-60) describes a retrieval design ("retrieval injects only the lines for the APIs a plan touches") but the Minecraft build service does not use it; that path belongs to Valheim/Terraria knowledge files (lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts). Two knowledge systems.
- Size: sheet + rules is roughly 4-5k tokens per build (UNVERIFIED estimate from 15 KB).

## (c) Where the new pieces plug in

1. **ModSpec / project model**: new typed JSON stored per project. Natural home: a new table keyed by `rootBuildId` (same convention as `CyrusModPage.rootBuildId @unique`, schema.prisma:9171) and a per-revision snapshot, not more fields in `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON (that column is already overloaded: per-build model/attachments + per-project title/listing, meta.ts:16-33). Revision identity today = `ModBuild.id`; so "revision" should reference `ModBuild.id` (one row per build/spec snapshot).
2. **Build request**: `POST /builds` body and `lib/modbuilder/create.ts:30-115` (builds the service payload; `attachmentIds` -> `images`). Add `spec` and `assets` here; service side `server.js:866` handler and `initialPrompt/changePrompt` (prompts.js:77-100) to pass the spec as a file in the workspace (e.g. `spec.json`, allowed write area is `src/main/**` + `modbuilder.json`, prompts.js rule 2).
3. **Workspace/packaging**: resources already land in the jar from `src/main/resources/**` (jar built from javac output dir, server.js:521, UNVERIFIED whether resources are copied into `out/` before `jar`; see server.js ~518 "Resources (plugin.yml, config.yml, ...)"). A resource pack must be a SEPARATE zip artifact (alongside `artifact.jar`, `jarPath` in `ModBuild`, schema.prisma `jarPath/jarSha256`). `ModBuild` has no pack columns; stored jars at `MODBUILD_DIR/<id>.jar` (lib/modbuilder/store.ts:16-17). Add `packPath/packSha1` or a generic `ModBuildArtifact` table.
4. **Install**: `lib/mods/installers/minecraft.ts` `place()` returns `PlacedFile[]` of arbitrary paths (types.ts), so the engine can already write extra files with backup/rollback; `resolveCyrus` (installers/cyrus.ts:45) returns the jar via `loadCyrusJar` (cyrus-mods/registry.ts:54). Add a second package (pack zip) there.
5. **DB**: new tables (see 1), and `GameMod`/`ServerMod` already model per-server installs (schema.prisma:3610).
6. **NxLabs generator**: `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts:170 buildModDoc(chain)` creates the page doc from builds; add an "assets" section sourced from the spec; `CyrusModMedia`/`ModMedia` exist for images (schema.prisma:3800, 9342).
7. **Studio UI state**: client store keeps a studio-side `Mod`/`ModVersion` model (lib/cyrus/types.ts, real.ts maps ModBuild -> Mod, real.ts:1-14); files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`.

## (d) Can the Mods engine deliver a resource pack and set server.properties on a customer's itzg server?

- Layout: Minecraft servers are itzg/minecraft-server in a Docker container named `mc` on a customer VM; `/opt/mc` on the VM = container `/data`; env in `/root/mc.env`; run flags `-v /opt/mc:/data --env-file /root/mc.env` (worker/game-config.ts:782, installers/minecraft.ts header). Files are reached over SSH (`SshGuestFs`, lib/modbuilder/install.ts:56-61; lib/mods/guest-fs.ts).
- **Placing a pack file**: yes, mechanically (PlacedFile path under `/opt/mc`), but a Minecraft `resource-pack` setting needs an **HTTP(S) URL** and SHA-1; a local file on the server is not served (no web server in the container). So the pack zip must be hosted by Nxeon (the NX Labs mirror exists, installers/cyrus.ts doc comment; `lib/mods/mirror.ts`; UNVERIFIED that it serves arbitrary public URLs).
- **Setting server.properties**: possible. `applyMinecraft` finds `server.properties`, rewrites keys with `updateKeyValue` via SFTP (worker/game-config.ts:793-826). But **no resource-pack field exists** in the game-config schema (grep for `resource-pack|RESOURCE_PACK` returned nothing in lib/ or worker/ apart from unrelated "Resource Packs" category labels: lib/mods-browse.ts:99, installers/minecraft.ts:51-55 which actively marks resource packs "unsupported: run on players' own game"). itzg also supports env vars `RESOURCE_PACK`/`RESOURCE_PACK_SHA1`/`RESOURCE_PACK_ENFORCE` (UNVERIFIED from memory, not opened); since the container is built from `mc.env` and recreated on version change (worker/game-config.ts:880-900), env vs file precedence must be settled by testing.
- The engine has no "post-install config step" hook, no uninstall of properties (engine uninstall removes files it placed, engine.ts:442), and `restartRequired: true` (installers/minecraft.ts:~495). Needed: a typed "server settings patch" operation recorded in the state file so uninstall can revert it.
- Alternative: Paper plugin generated by Cyrus calling `Player#setResourcePack(url, sha1bytes, prompt, force)` on join (needs no server.properties change; uses the plugin path that already works). Also requires the URL to be reachable. Note the safety scan forbids networking for the plugin itself (rules/net-policy.json, prompts rule 5), but setResourcePack only hands a URL to the client (UNVERIFIED whether scan.js flags it).

## (e) What `textures/` and `sfx.ts` actually do

- `lib/cyrus/textures/*` (7 files, ~350 lines): `dsl.ts` = declarative `TextureSpec` (16/32/64 px, palette, <=400 ops: fill/px/rect/line/circle/poly/gradient/noise/shade/outline); `render.ts` = deterministic RGBA rasteriser; `png.ts` encoder; `zip.ts`; `pack.ts` `buildPack()` = 1-24 **item** textures -> `assets/<ns>/{textures/item,models/item,items}/<name>` (1.21.4+ `items/` model definitions for `setItemModel`) + pack.mcmeta + sha1. Nothing else: no mobs/blocks/entity models/animations/GUI/particles/sounds.json. **Not wired to the build pipeline or UI**: only used by the marketing demo (`components/cyrus/marketing/PixelForge.tsx:4-6`) and a unit test (`test/cyrus-textures.test.ts`). `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x (returns 75; see E-versions.md).
- `lib/cyrus/sfx.ts` (155 lines): **UI feedback sounds** synthesised in the browser with Web Audio (tick, ping, whoosh, stage, success, error, thump), off by default, `localStorage "cyrus-sfx"`; imported only by `lib/cyrus/fx.ts:12` and `CyrusDemo.tsx:26`. It cannot produce game sound effects and writes no files. So "Sound Studio" has no code beyond this; the owner's 514-MP3 library is not referenced anywhere in code (no grep hits needed; UNVERIFIED negative).
- Studio copy still says coming soon (`components/cyrus/marketing/StudioArt.tsx` matched the "coming soon" grep).

## (f) Plan-tier reading and where to gate asset features

- `TOKEN_TIERS = free|katara|saka|all` (lib/cyrus/tokens/config.ts:10), `PLAN_TIERS` without free (:12). Effective tier: `effectiveTier({plan, override, ...})` (tokens/economy.ts:44-59; handles active/trialing/past_due/canceled windows and admin override); loader `tierOf(userId)` (tokens/access.ts:37). Tier -> allowed models only: `TIER_MODELS` (economy.ts:15-20), `canUseModel` (:25).
- Single enforcement point for builds: `gateBuild` (tokens/builds.ts:25-50), called once from `lib/modbuilder/create.ts:72`. It is only active when `tokensActiveFor` (live flag or preview list, access.ts:18-27); otherwise builds pass through untracked.
- Gate asset features there: extend `gateBuild`'s input with requested asset features and return a new `code` (e.g. `asset_locked`), and read the tier via `tierOf` for UI (`buildTokenState`, tokens/state.ts:13-26). Model names (katara/saka/yakko) double as tier names in the UI and in `engine/kit.ts:365 MODEL_NAME`; do not conflate with feature tiers. No feature-flag table keyed by tier exists (UNVERIFIED beyond grep of tierOf/canUseModel usage).
- Note: NxLabs publication has its own gate (lib/cyrus/public-gate.ts, lib/cyrus-mods/gate.ts); asset licensing checks (owner's SFX licence) should go there.

## (g) Ranked missing pieces / debt that will hurt scaling

1. **No project/spec/asset data model** and `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON overloaded; revisions are build rows with no diff/rollback of assets (schema.prisma:8590; meta.ts). Blocks everything below.
2. **Version support is hardcoded in 4+ places** and tied to JDK 21/`--release 21`/Gradle template toolchain 21 (types.ts:3, Dockerfile:11,49, server.js:513, template/build.gradle.kts:21-25). 26.x cannot be added without a registry + JDK 25 (E-versions.md).
3. **Knowledge = whole-sheet injection per version, hand-generated, no 26.x**; two incompatible knowledge systems (`KnowledgePack` retrieval vs services sheets). Sheets will not scale to creatures/models/GUI/particles/datapack APIs; token cost per build rises with every addition.
4. **Asset pipeline missing end-to-end**: textures only items, unwired; no model/entity/animation/sound generation; no sounds.json; sfx.ts is UI-only; pack format table wrong for 26.x.
5. **Delivery path for client assets missing**: no resource-pack URL hosting, no `resource-pack`/sha1 config field, no pack artifact in `ModBuild`, engine has no settings-patch step; installer marks resource packs unsupported (installers/minecraft.ts:55).
6. **Plugin-only ceiling**: Paper-plugin sandbox (no reflection/NMS/networking rules) cannot express custom mobs with custom models, blocks, dimensions without datapacks/resource packs; datapack placement exists in the installer (installers/minecraft.ts:455-465) but the generator never produces datapacks (UNVERIFIED but no code does).
7. **No mod-vs-mod conflict engine or mod packs**: engine handles file ownership only (engine.ts:281); no pack/bundle entity.
8. **No import-your-own-mod flow** (no code, no scanner path for foreign jars; scan.js works on freshly compiled bytecode in the workspace).
9. **Eval coverage thin**: 30 prompts (13 runtime-loaded) on 1.21.x only; rtcheck uses `eclipse-temurin:21-jre`, mineflayer bot, per-version Paper jars on the build VM (eval/rtcheck.py:1-15); no assets, no multi-version matrix, ops live on a single VM (`/root/...` paths, run_eval.py reads `/root/modbuilder.env`).
10. **Simulated template engine (1701 lines) alongside the real path** — risk of divergence and confusion for non-Minecraft games (lib/cyrus/engine/templates.ts).
11. **Single build VM**: concurrency 2, 20 min timeout, `/data` on one host (server.js:44-60); no queue/scale-out story (UNVERIFIED beyond defaults).
12. **Tier model conflation**: plans gate models, not features; `gateBuild` only tracks when economy is live.

## Could not determine
Whether `jar` includes `src/main/resources/**` via an explicit copy (read only lines ~511-521, ~518 comment); the NX Labs mirror's ability to host public pack URLs; whether scan.js flags `setResourcePack`; itzg env/file precedence; any use of the 514-MP3 library in code (not searched beyond the Cyrus dirs).

content.content:
# A. What a Paper plugin + server-pushed resource pack (+ datapack) can create on a VANILLA Java client

Date 2026-10-10. Web budget: 20 pages/searches used (several 404). Labels: VERIFIED (url) = opened; UNVERIFIED = memory/inference, re-check before building. Internal facts from E-versions.md / G-gaps.md (resource packs unsupported by installer; no pack hosting, no resource-pack server setting yet).

## 0. The enabling primitives (what exists today)
- **Item model definitions** (`assets/<ns>/items/*.json`, bound with the `item_model` component): types model/composite/condition/select/range_dispatch/special/empty; added 1.21.4, extended through 26.x. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Items_model_definition). This replaced the old "overrides in the item model json" approach. Pre-1.21.4 versions (1.21.1) still need legacy `custom_model_data` int overrides: UNVERIFIED but well known; Cyrus supports 1.21.1 so the pack builder needs two emitters.
- **Data component API in Paper** (CUSTOM_MODEL_DATA, LORE, ENCHANTMENTS, RARITY, MAX_DAMAGE, EQUIPPABLE, GLIDER shown; item_model/food/consumable/weapon/tool/use_cooldown referenced). Docs warn "may experience breaking changes on version updates... backwards compatibility is not promised". VERIFIED (https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/data-component-api/). `@Experimental` removed in 26.3: VERIFIED internally (E-versions.md, papermc.io/news/26-3).
- **Registry mutation at bootstrap** (`RegistryEvents`, `compose()` / `entryAdd()`; example is enchantments; Paper plugin + `paper-plugin.yml` only; errors abort startup; compose fires after built-in/datapack content loads). VERIFIED (https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/registries/). Full list of writable registries: not determined.
- **Lifecycle API**: Brigadier commands, registry modification, datapack management at bootstrap. VERIFIED (https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/lifecycle/).
- **Datapacks shipped inside a plugin jar** (unzipped folder under resources, `DatapackRegistrar#discoverPack(URI,id)` in `DATAPACK_DISCOVERY`; pack name `<Plugin>/<id>`; discovery ignores enabled state). VERIFIED (https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/lifecycle/datapacks/). Runtime reload not documented there.
- **Pack format numbers** per version: see E-versions.md (VERIFIED minecraft.wiki/w/Pack_format). 26.x client needs correct `min_format/max_format`; current `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x.
- **Server-pushed pack**: `resource-pack` + sha1 in server.properties or Paper `Player#setResourcePack`; players get the accept prompt, no manual download. UNVERIFIED here (standard behaviour); Nxeon must host the zip over HTTPS (G-gaps section d).

## 1. Matrix per content type
Legend: V = vanilla-possible with pack/datapack. M = needs client mod. AI = how reliably an AI can generate it from a prompt (High/Med/Low).

| Content | Technique today | V / M | Version sensitivity | AI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Custom mobs (model, texture, animation)** | Invisible/base vanilla mob (hitbox, AI, attributes, drops) + `item_display` / `block_display` entities carrying bbmodel bones as `item_model` items, animated by interpolating transformations each tick; Interaction entity for hitboxes. Libraries (below) do this. Custom sounds via `sounds.json`. UNVERIFIED mechanics; BetterModel describes "Bedrock model engine... BlockBench models... Molang animations, IK" and auto pack generation VERIFIED (github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel) | V (display-entity based; costs server CPU/packets per mob). True new entity type: M | Display entity transformation API stable since 1.19.4; item_model route needs 1.21.4+ (BetterModel lists 1.21.4 to 26.3.x, VERIFIED same URL) so **1.21.1 is not covered**. | Med: AI can write behaviour (Paper API); generating a rigged animated bbmodel from a prompt is Low-Med (simple cube-rig + idle/walk/attack from a spec = feasible, organic models = poor). |
| **Custom items: weapons (gun), tools, food, armor** | Item = base material + components: `item_model`, `custom_model_data`, `consumable`, `food`, `tool`, `weapon`, `equippable` (armor with custom `equipment` asset json), `use_cooldown`, attribute modifiers, PDC tag for logic. Gun = right-click event, hitscan ray trace or Snowball/Arrow projectile, cooldown, particles/sounds, ammo in PDC; recoil/ADS via model swap with `condition`/`select` item model, or FOV trick with slowness (UNVERIFIED hack). | V | Components exist from 1.20.5; `item_model` 1.21.2+, `consumable/equippable/use_cooldown` 1.21.2+, `weapon` 1.21.5+ (UNVERIFIED dates). Paper API surfaces differ by version; data component API breaks without notice (VERIFIED above). 3D held model animation (reload) needs per-state models only: no true bone animation without display entities. | **High** for logic; Med for art (needs Texture Studio output: flat 16x16/32x32 icon + simple 3D model). |
| **Custom blocks (incl. machines)** | (a) Re-purpose note block (800 states), tripwire, chorus plant, mushroom blocks and give each a model through blockstate overrides; cancel vanilla behaviour in events (what Oraxen/Nexo/CraftEngine do; Oraxen lists full/string/chorus/stair/slab/door/trapdoor/grate/bulb variants VERIFIED github.com/oraxen/oraxen). (b) Furniture/machine = `item_display` + Interaction entity on top of a barrier/light block. Machine logic = tile data in PDC/DB + ticking in the plugin; GUI via inventory menu. | V, but a limited pool of block states (~800 note-block states + a few thousand across others) and no new hardness/sound/light properties without hacks; custom drop/break speed needs mining-fatigue/packet tricks (UNVERIFIED). Real new block types: M | Blockstate-based approach is stable but each MC version can change which states are "safe" (note block change in 1.20.x mapping). Tracked by lib; high maintenance. | Med. AI can specify; correctness of state allocation + collisions with pack is the fragile part, so generate through a library/registry, never by hand. |
| **HUDs / overlays** | (1) Action bar text in a custom `font` with bitmap glyphs and negative-space characters to position (ascent/height tricks). (2) Boss bar title as HUD strip (multiple bars). (3) Title/subtitle. (4) Sidebar scoreboard with hidden numbers. (5) Core-shader overrides (e.g. `rendertype_text`) for pixel-exact UI, colour-coded transparency flags. UNVERIFIED (community-standard; Oraxen "Glyphs/HUD" VERIFIED url above). | V (all text-based or shader-based on vanilla client) | **Highest risk**: core shaders change format between versions (many packs re-released for 26.1, VERIFIED weakly via search results listing 26.1 shader packs) and break under Sodium/Iris-style client mods (UNVERIFIED). BetterModel advertises "zero reliance on core shaders" (VERIFIED) = trend is to avoid them. Font glyph route is more stable across versions. | Glyph HUD: Med-High if Cyrus ships a tested helper lib (AI calls `Hud.show(player,id,value)`); raw shader writing: Low, avoid. |
| **Custom GUIs / menus** | Chest/other `MenuType` inventory with a **title containing a bitmap glyph** that paints a texture over the container area (negative-space shifts), item slots using `item_model` icons, hidden tooltips. Newer: native **Dialog** screens (1.21.6+, server-sent, UNVERIFIED) give real buttons/inputs without art. | V (art limited to the container grid + glyph overlay) | Menu API stable; container title font texture heights capped; dialog API only 1.21.6+ (UNVERIFIED, check Paper docs). | High for logic/layout; Med for art. |
| **Particles** | Vanilla particle types via API (incl. DUST colour/size, ITEM, BLOCK, VIBRATION, TRAIL...). Custom look: (a) override a rarely used vanilla particle's texture in the pack, (b) `text_display`/`item_display` quads animated server-side. UNVERIFIED | V (custom shapes only via display entities / replaced textures) | Particle enum/registry changed in recent versions (E-versions: enum to registry changes UNVERIFIED). | High |
| **Enchantments** | Data-driven registry since 1.21: datapack JSON `enchantment/*.json` or Paper `RegistryEvents` compose at bootstrap (VERIFIED registries URL). Effects limited to vanilla effect components; custom behaviour = plugin listeners keyed on the enchant. | V | JSON schema shifts almost every version (UNVERIFIED); enchant is a registry object on 1.21+, enum before. | Med-High with schema-driven generator (see A2). |
| **Recipes** | Bukkit Recipe API (shaped/shapeless/smelting/stonecutter/smithing, `ExactChoice` for custom items) or datapack JSON. | V | Datapack recipe result/ingredient format changed in 1.20.5/1.21.2 (UNVERIFIED). | **High** |
| **Advancements** | Datapack JSON (criteria triggers + display with `item_model` icon) or Paper advancement API (UNVERIFIED). | V (custom background/icon via pack) | Folder names singular since 1.21 (VERIFIED minecraft.wiki/w/Data_pack). | High |
| **Bosses** | Strong base mob (or model-engine mob) + Paper `BossBar` + phases/abilities/loot in plugin; arena via structure/command. | V | none specific | High |
| **Abilities / projectiles** | Paper events + scheduler, raycasts, Snowball/Arrow/Display-entity projectiles, particles, sounds, potion effects. | V | Scheduler differences Folia/Paper (UNVERIFIED). | **High** |
| **Commands** | Brigadier Commands API via lifecycle event (VERIFIED lifecycle URL); clients get tab completion. | V | Command API moved from plugin.yml commands to lifecycle; 26.x unverified (E-versions). | High |
| **Music / ambience / SFX** | `sounds.json` + .ogg in pack; `jukebox_song` datapack registry for discs; ambient via scheduled `playSound` / biome ambient sounds in datapack. | V | `sounds.json` stable. | High (assets from Sound Studio). |
| **Biomes / structures / worldgen** | Datapack JSON: `worldgen/biome`, `configured_feature`, `placed_feature`, `structure`, `template_pool`, `noise_settings`, `dimension`, `dimension_type`. Server syncs registries so a vanilla client can join (UNVERIFIED but well established). Structure NBT files in `structure/`. Biomes: custom fog/sky/water/grass colours, spawn tables, features, music. | V for biomes, structures, ore/tree features, new dimensions using vanilla noise/terrain tech; **not** V: new block types, custom sky *rendering* (dimension_type `effect` limited to vanilla set, UNVERIFIED), custom biome *names* on the client (F3 shows id) | Worldgen datapack JSON changes most between versions (26.x added things, UNVERIFIED). `/reload` does NOT reload worldgen; needs restart (VERIFIED minecraft.wiki/w/Data_pack). New biome only generates in new chunks. | Med with a schema-driven generator + vanilla-parameter templates; Low for hand-written noise settings / structure NBT. See A2. |

## 2. Client-mod-only list (cannot be done on a vanilla client)
- New block types with arbitrary properties, new entity types with native models/animations, true custom blocks beyond the reusable-state pool.
- Arbitrary HUD widgets/GUI screens with real controls and free layout (Dialog API gives only form-like screens).
- Custom keybinds, mouse capture, camera control, client-side prediction (smooth gun recoil).
- New dimension sky/cloud/fog *renderers*; custom shaders that need new vertex formats; post-processing outside the shipped pipeline mechanism (UNVERIFIED how much `post_effect`/core shaders allow on 26.x).
- Anything requiring new client code paths (new GUI sliders, minimap, custom render of player model).
Fabric/NeoForge client-mod route: out of scope for Cyrus today; Nxeon would need to ship players a client mod pack = adoption friction.

## 3. Libraries and licences (can Nxeon depend on / bundle?)
| Library | Area | Licence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BetterModel** | bbmodel mobs/props/player models, animations, auto pack | **MIT** VERIFIED (github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel); Bukkit servers + Fabric; 1.21.4 to 26.3.x | **Adopt**: can be bundled or required as a dependency; keep MIT notice. Best fit for the "banshee" mob use case. |
| **CraftEngine** (Xiao-MoMi) | custom blocks/items/furniture/GUI/recipes via config | **GPL-3.0** community edition; premium edition sold separately VERIFIED (github.com/Xiao-MoMi/craft-engine) | **Avoid as a bundled dependency** (GPL); study as design reference only. Running it as a separate server plugin the customer installs is legally cleaner than linking, but Nxeon-generated jars must not link to its API. |
| **Oraxen** | items, blocks, glyphs/HUD, pack hosting | Paid (Spigot/BuiltByBit), source visible with LICENSE.md terms, "forks only for PRs" VERIFIED (github.com/oraxen/oraxen) | **Avoid**: cannot redistribute. |
| **Nexo** | items, blocks, armor, furniture, auto pack | Paid; docs say 1.21.1 to 1.21.11 (VERIFIED via search result excerpt, nexomc.com docs) ; GitHub page 404; terms UNVERIFIED | **Avoid** (paid, per-server licence, 26.x unclear). |
| **ModelEngine R4** (Ticxo) | bbmodel mobs, MythicMobs integration | Paid, free demo limited; reported expensive; lists 1.19.4 to 26.2 on a re-host site (UNVERIFIED, mirror sites unreliable) | **Avoid** bundling; BetterModel is the open equivalent. |
| **MythicMobs** | mob skills/AI config | Free base + paid Premium (UNVERIFIED; official page not opened, GitLab link needs login) | **Avoid** dependency; Cyrus generates Java behaviour itself. |
| **ItemsAdder** | all-in-one | Paid (UNVERIFIED) | Avoid. |
| **Blockbench** (editor) | model/animation authoring, bbmodel format | GPL-3.0 UNVERIFIED; the *file format* is JSON (reading it is fine) | Reference only: write our own bbmodel emitter, never embed the editor. |
Net: only BetterModel is a clean commercial dependency. Everything else (items, blocks, HUD glyph, pack builder, menus) should be a small **Cyrus runtime library** owned by Nxeon, because Cyrus-generated plugins are compiled against a frozen classpath and need a stable, versioned helper API anyway.

## 4. Ranked build order (value vs effort)
1. **Pack hosting + server-pushed pack + correct per-version pack_format** (S-M). Unblocks everything; installer currently marks packs unsupported.
2. **Items with custom art** via `item_model`/CMD, food/tool/weapon/armor components, recipes, sounds (M). Texture Studio output already exists in `lib/cyrus/textures`; biggest "wow per effort"; weapons/guns high AI reliability.
3. **Abilities/projectiles/bosses/commands/enchant/advancements** with vanilla-only assets (S, mostly prompt + sheet work).
4. **Custom mobs on BetterModel** (L): bbmodel emitter from Texture Studio spec, 1.21.4+ only, multi-sound set. Highest marketing value; heavy generation risk.
5. **Glyph-based HUD + GUI menus helper lib** (M): fonts/negative-space helper, Dialog where available; no core shaders.
6. **Datapack studio** for biomes/structures/enchants (L, see A2).
7. **Custom blocks/machines** (L): state-pool allocator + display-entity furniture; maintenance-heavy.
8. **Core-shader effects** (L, last or never): fragile across 26.x and client mods.

## 5. Gaps / not determined
Writable-registry list; Nexo/ModelEngine/MythicMobs official licence text; exact 26.x client behaviour for shaders and font glyph limits; Dialog API Paper availability; 1.21.1 item_model route (must use legacy CMD).
# A2. Data pack studio: formats, loading, validation, build-vs-adopt

Date 2026-10-10. Labels: VERIFIED (url) = opened; UNVERIFIED = memory/inference.

## 1. Formats per version
- Folder names are **singular** in current versions: `function/`, `loot_table/`, `recipe/`, `advancement/`, `tags/item|block|entity_type/`; content dirs `worldgen/`, `dimension/`, `enchantment/`, `damage_type/`, `jukebox_song/`. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_pack). The plural-to-singular rename happened in 1.21 (1.21.1 already singular; pre-1.21 plural) UNVERIFIED for exact release; Cyrus' floor is 1.21.1 so it only ever needs singular.
- `pack.mcmeta`: since 1.21.9 uses `min_format` / `max_format` as `[major, minor]` (e.g. `[88, 0]`) and supports `overlays` for per-version content. VERIFIED (same URL). Older (<1.21.9) use `pack_format` (+ `supported_formats`): UNVERIFIED detail.
- Data pack format numbers (VERIFIED, minecraft.wiki/w/Pack_format, via E-versions.md): 1.21.1 = 48; 1.21.4 = 61; 1.21.7-8 = 81; 1.21.9-10 = 88.0; 1.21.11 = 94.1; 26.1-26.1.2 = 101.1; 26.2 = 107.1; 26.3 = 121.0.
- Practical consequence: Cyrus' supported set 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 1.21.11 (+26.x) spans **four different datapack schemas and two mcmeta styles**. Use `overlays` (VERIFIED to exist) only where one pack must span versions; otherwise emit one pack per target version from one version-neutral spec.
- JSON schema drift that matters (UNVERIFIED, must be proven by validating against each version): recipe `result` object + item-stack components (1.20.5+), loot function names/predicates (components replaced NBT in 1.20.5), enchantment data-driven format (1.21), item predicate rewrite in advancements/loot (1.21.5), attribute modifier ids (1.21), worldgen noise/density function tweaks per release. Never trust the model's memory of these.

## 2. Schemas by content
| Data type | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Recipes | `recipe/*.json` | shaped, shapeless, smelting/blasting/smoking/campfire, stonecutting, smithing_transform/trim, crafting_transform. Bukkit API is an alternative for plugins. |
| Loot tables | `loot_table/**` | pools, entries, functions, conditions; types: block, entity, chest, gift, fishing... |
| Advancements | `advancement/**` | criteria triggers, display, rewards, parent chain. |
| Tags | `tags/<registry>/**` | item/block/entity_type/biome/enchantment etc.; `replace:false` merges. |
| Functions | `function/**.mcfunction` | command text; `#minecraft:tick` / `#minecraft:load` tags run them. |
| Enchantments | `enchantment/*.json` | data-driven since 1.21; also writable from Paper bootstrap `RegistryEvents.compose()` (VERIFIED https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/registries/). |
| Worldgen | `worldgen/biome`, `configured_feature`, `placed_feature`, `structure`, `structure_set`, `template_pool`, `processor_list`, `noise_settings`, `density_function`, `world_preset`; plus `dimension`, `dimension_type`; structure NBT in `structure/` | Structures need binary NBT templates. |
Machine-readable truth for all of these: **vanilla-mcdoc** (MIT; schemas for datapack and resource pack JSON/NBT, version-aware). VERIFIED (https://github.com/SpyglassMC/vanilla-mcdoc).

## 3. How Paper loads / reloads
- Plugin-shipped packs: unzipped folder in the jar resources, `DatapackRegistrar#discoverPack(URI,id)` inside the `DATAPACK_DISCOVERY` lifecycle event from a `PluginBootstrap` (needs `paper-plugin.yml`); loaded pack name `<Plugin>/<id>`; discovery does not decide whether the pack is enabled, check with `/datapack list enabled`. VERIFIED (https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/lifecycle/datapacks/). Runtime reload: not documented there (UNVERIFIED conclusion: discovery is boot-time).
- World packs: drop into `<world>/datapacks/` (zip or folder) - UNVERIFIED but standard; Cyrus installer already places datapacks (G-gaps :455-465).
- `/reload` re-reads recipes, loot tables, advancements, functions, tags but **not worldgen**; worldgen changes need a restart. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_pack). New biomes/structures only appear in chunks generated after load (UNVERIFIED). A new dimension needs restart + world creation.
- Custom registry content from Java: `RegistryEvents` `compose()`/`entryAdd()` fire after vanilla/datapack content loads; errors abort startup; Paper plugin only. VERIFIED (registries URL).
- Datapack worldgen on a customer's existing world can produce chunk borders and biome-id mismatch (UNVERIFIED); studio should default to "new dimension / new world" for big worldgen and warn for existing worlds.

## 4. Validators and open-source generators
| Tool | What | Licence | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **misode.github.io** | Generators for loot tables, recipes, advancements, worldgen, dimension, predicates; supports 1.15-1.21 + 26.1 per README | **MIT** VERIFIED (https://github.com/misode/misode.github.io) | Reference UI/logic; can be forked/self-hosted; 26.2/26.3 coverage unverified. Uses mcdoc schemas in `public/mcdoc`. |
| **vanilla-mcdoc** | Authoritative schemas (CODEC/JSON/NBT) | **MIT** VERIFIED | **Adopt as the schema source** for validator + type generation. |
| **Spyglass** (SpyglassMC core / language server) | Parses mcdoc, validates datapack text | licence UNVERIFIED (believed MIT) | Candidate engine for a Node-based CLI validator; confirm licence + 26.x support. |
| **misode/mcmeta** | Per-version vanilla data, registries, reports | UNVERIFIED | Source of version-accurate registry id lists. |
| **Vanilla data generator** (`java -DbundlerMainClass=net.minecraft.data.Main -jar server.jar --server`) | Dumps vanilla data pack + registries/command-tree reports; flags `--server`, `--dev`, `--input` documented. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial:Running_the_data_generator). A `--validate` flag is NOT confirmed there (UNVERIFIED). | Mojang EULA; run only on our build host, do not redistribute output | Generate per-version registry id lists (blocks, items, entity types, sounds, biomes, features) that the generator uses to reject unknown ids. |
Mojang's own jar is the ultimate validator (see section 5).

## 5. Headless load-test (proposed; none of it run)
1. Static: JSON parse + mcdoc/schema validation + id existence check against the per-version registry dump + pack.mcmeta format check. Fast, deterministic, no JVM.
2. Dynamic: boot the real Paper jar for the target version in a throwaway container (the build service already compiles against the real jars; the same image family can start one) with the pack in `world/datapacks` (or bundled in a test plugin), flat/void world, RCON enabled. UNVERIFIED design:
   - Parse startup log for datapack load errors (Minecraft logs failed resources as "Couldn't parse data file ..." / "Failed to load datapack" - UNVERIFIED exact strings; build the matcher by deliberately breaking a pack on each version).
   - `datapack list enabled` shows it loaded; `reload` then re-check; `recipe give @a *`/`advancement grant` to prove they resolve; `function ns:test` and read RCON replies; `loot spawn`/`loot give` to exercise tables; `place feature|structure|template` and `locate biome` for worldgen; `execute in <dimension> run ...` for dimensions.
   - Boot time ~tens of seconds per version; budget one test per supported version per build. Cost is CPU/time on the build VM, not tokens.
3. Regression: keep a golden corpus of known-good packs per version (misode examples + vanilla dump) to detect when the validator itself drifts on a new release.

## 6. What the AI writes vs what a generator produces
- **AI writes**: the intent as a small typed *spec* (e.g. `{type:"recipe", shape:[...], ingredients, result}`), `.mcfunction` command logic (short, line-oriented, validated against the command tree from the data generator), names/lore/text, balance numbers, loot weights, and the Java glue for enchant/ability behaviour.
- **Schema-driven generator produces**: all JSON for recipe, loot_table, advancement, tags, enchantment, damage_type, jukebox_song, biome, features, dimension, `pack.mcmeta`, overlays, folder layout - from the spec, per version, using the mcdoc-derived types and registry dumps. The model should never emit raw version-specific JSON for these.
- **Programmatic builders (not LLM)**: structure NBT (build a block grid or Paper `StructureManager` capture from a template, write gzip NBT), noise settings / density functions (parameterised presets: "tropical-ish", "flat plains+custom ores"; expose a few knobs), biome colour/precipitation/spawn tables from presets.
- AI is reliable for recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments (via spec). It is unreliable for hand-written worldgen noise, structure jigsaw pools, and any field name from memory across versions.

## 7. MVP scope
1. Spec types: recipe, loot_table, advancement, tag, function, enchantment, jukebox_song/sound event. (No worldgen in MVP.)
2. Per-version emitters for 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11, 26.x (one table of format numbers, one adapter per schema delta).
3. Static validator (schema + registry ids) + dynamic Paper boot test per target version in CI of the build service.
4. Output either (a) plugin-bundled pack via `DATAPACK_DISCOVERY` or (b) standalone zip placed by the installer; plus a Studio editor that shows/edits the spec and the generated JSON (misode-style forms).
5. Phase 2: biomes (preset + colours), custom ore/tree features, simple structures from a block grid, new dimension from preset.

## 8. Build vs adopt, effort
| Item | Decision | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Schema source | Adopt vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); pin per-version snapshot | S |
| Registry/id dump per version | Build script around Mojang data generator on build host | S-M |
| Spec -> JSON generators (7 types x 5 version adapters) | Build (mcdoc types give structure; adapters hand-tuned) | M |
| Static validator | Adopt Spyglass core if licence OK, else Build thin JSON-schema layer from mcdoc | M |
| Studio UI | Reuse patterns from misode (MIT) but build in Nxeon theme; do not iframe misode | M |
| Dynamic headless load test | Build (RCON harness on existing build VM) | M |
| Worldgen presets + structure NBT builder | Build | L |
| Overlays/multi-version single pack | Build later (VERIFIED feature exists) | S |

## 9. Not determined
Spyglass and mcmeta licences; whether the vanilla data generator has a usable validation mode; exact error strings for load failures; 26.2/26.3 coverage in misode and mcdoc; Paper runtime datapack reload semantics; exact version where folders became singular.

# B-models: automatic custom creature + weapon models for Cyrus (vanilla client, Paper, server-pushed pack)
Date 2026-10-10. Read-only research, 13 pages opened. VERIFIED = opened; UNVERIFIED = memory/inference.

## 1. Blockbench and the .bbmodel format
- App licence: GPL-3.0 source; plugins/themes using the Blockbench API are exempt and may be proprietary or paid. VERIFIED (https://github.com/JannisX11/blockbench). Implication: Nxeon must not embed/redistribute the Blockbench app in its product, but it can write .bbmodel files and let customers open them in the (free) app/web app. Using the app as a headless renderer/separate process is a licence question for counsel: UNVERIFIED.
- .bbmodel is JSON ("There is no complete specification of the JSON format at this point in time"; read examples and `js/formats/bbmodel.js`). VERIFIED (https://blockbench.net/wiki/docs/bbmodel). So the format is readable but not formally specified or licensed as a standard. Risk: it changes. Format 5.0 (Blockbench 5.0, 2025-10-12) split `groups` from `outliner` and fixed inverted X position / X,Y rotation keyframe values. Cyrus must emit one pinned format_version and golden-test it against BetterModel.
- Skeleton: `format_version, name, resolution{width,height}, textures[{name,source:data:image/png;base64}], elements[{from,to,rotation,faces,uv}], groups[{uuid,name,children}], outliner[...], animations[{name,loop,length,animators[{channel position|rotation|scale, keyframes[]}]}]`. VERIFIED (same URL; skeleton from the page summary, keyframe field names beyond that UNVERIFIED, confirm from a real file).
- Java block/item model JSON: elements limited to from/to in -16..32; rotation single axis, 22.5 degree steps within -45..45, optional rescale; `display` transforms per context; since 1.21.4 block and item models are not distinguished internally. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Model). Keyframe animations are NOT part of vanilla block/item models; they exist only as .bbmodel data interpreted by a server-side engine (below).
- Item models 1.21.4 -> 26.x: 1.21.4 introduced `assets/<ns>/items/<id>.json` selected by the `item_model` data component, with types model, composite, select, range_dispatch (can switch on custom_model_data, use_duration, display_context, damage, etc.). 26.1 added a `transformation` field plus special models (bell, book, end_cube); 26.2 removed bed/standing_sign/hanging_sign special types; 26.3 removed the `map_color` tint source. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Items_model_definition). The pre-1.21.4 `overrides` + `CustomModelData` number path is the legacy route (UNVERIFIED detail); need pack-format-per-version builds for 1.21.1 vs 1.21.4+.

## 2. Server-side animated-model libraries
| Lib | Licence | Versions | Bundle? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BetterModel (toxicity188) | MIT VERIFIED | Modrinth lists 1.19.4, 1.20.x, 1.21.x, 26.1.x, 26.2, 26.3; Paper/Folia/Purpur/Spigot; updated "13 hours ago" (very active) VERIFIED (https://modrinth.com/mod/bettermodel). GitHub front page says 1.21.4-1.26.3 with Java 25+ (v3 branch); raw README on master says 1.20.5-1.21.11, Java 21. Conflicting; assume v3 needs Java 25 for 26.x. VERIFIED (https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel) | Both: `compileOnly io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-bukkit-api` (Maven Central, separate plugin) or `shadowJar` shading. VERIFIED (raw README) | Built on `item-display` packets; cubes, meshes, locators; animations with Molang + IK; per-player animation; custom hitbox; player-skin models; auto resource-pack generation; merge guides for Oraxen/ItemsAdder/Nexo/CraftEngine; async, "designed for high-traffic". 1,629 commits. No published entity-count numbers found. |
| ModelEngine R4 (Ticxo, sold via MythicCraft) | Proprietary, $39.99, no redistribution terms visible; closed, "very limited API" per BetterModel author VERIFIED (https://mythiccraft.io/index.php?resources/model-engine%E2%80%94ultimate-entity-model-manager-1-19-4-1-21-11.1213/) | 1.19-1.21.11, 26.1, 26.2; updated 2026-09-26 | No; must be bought per server (licence per server/redistribution UNVERIFIED) | Industry standard, MythicMobs integration. Avoid: cost, closed, cannot pre-install for customers without a licence deal. |
| FreeMinecraftModels (MagmaGuy) | GPL-3.0-only VERIFIED (https://modrinth.com/project/free-minecraft-models) | 1.18.x-26.3, standalone, updated last week | No: GPL would taint a bundled proprietary jar; separate-process/plugin use is a legal grey area | Lua scripting, furniture, animations. Avoid as a dependency. |
| Display entities directly (vanilla) | n/a | all 1.19.4+ | built in | item_display shows any `item_model`; interpolation via `start_interpolation` + `interpolation_duration`; no hitbox/collision/sound; count toward entity count. VERIFIED (https://minecraft.wiki/w/Display). A hand-rolled engine needs Interaction/base entity for hitbox. |
| Armor-stand engines (old ModelEngine, ModelAPI) | various | legacy | - | Avoid; superseded. |

API shape (BetterModel): `BetterModel.model("id").map(r -> r.create(entity, TrackerModifier.DEFAULT))`, `tracker.animate("attack", AnimationModifier.DEFAULT_WITH_PLAY_ONCE, cb)`, DummyTracker for location-only models, per-player animations, `tracker.close()` required to remove a model. VERIFIED (https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/wiki/API-example). Models are read from `plugins/BetterModel/models/*.bbmodel`. VERIFIED (raw README).

Gaps I could not determine: BetterModel per-entity bone/viewer limits and tick cost; exact pack-merge behaviour when Nxeon also pushes its own pack; whether a mixed-version jar supports 1.21.1 (Modrinth list is broad; test). Plan a benchmark: N banshees x 20 bones x 20 viewers on a 4 GB node (S).

Can Nxeon pre-install? BetterModel: yes (MIT, free), install it as a managed system plugin on every Cyrus-enabled server, version-pinned per Minecraft version, generated plugins `depend: [BetterModel]`. Shading is allowed but duplicates the engine per mod and breaks pack merging; avoid. ModelEngine: only with a commercial agreement.

## 3. Automatic generation by an LLM
- The LLM should not emit raw .bbmodel (UUIDs, UV rects, keyframe maths = error-prone). It emits a compact RigSpec (section 4); deterministic Nxeon code compiles it to .bbmodel + PNG + animations. This also gives Texture Studio hooks (re-paint without re-rigging).
- Archetype templates (each = bone tree + default dimensions + animation presets): humanoid, quadruped, flyer/bird, floating ghost (banshee), serpent, spider/multi-leg, blob, plus prop/weapon (single bone). LLM picks archetype + overrides colour/size/features (horns, wings, tail, glow).
- UV: per-cuboid box-unwrap (Minecraft-style cross layout) auto-packed on one atlas (e.g. 64x64 / 128x128). Reuse existing `lib/cyrus/textures` pixel renderer by painting per-face palette regions + noise/gradients (UNVERIFIED how it fits; internal code not read).
- Procedural animation: library of parametric clips driven by bone roles (sine bob for idle/float, leg-swing for walk, wind-up + strike for attack, flinch + red flash for hurt, tilt + sink + fade for death). Compiler samples to keyframes at 0.05 s steps with linear/catmullrom interpolation. LLM only chooses clip type/amplitude/speed per role.
- Published approaches: BlockbenchMCP lets an AI drive the desktop Blockbench (bones+cubes, procedural textures, keyframes, screenshots for self-review); one report of a full GeckoLib bear (walk/run/sleep/attack) from one prompt. VERIFIED search result only; repo https://github.com/jasonjgardner/blockbench-mcp-project is Apache-2.0 sample project needing a running Blockbench desktop app, with a headless `blockbench-new-model` skill VERIFIED. Useful as design inspiration/QA, not as a server dependency (GUI app, GPL). No published "AI to Paper animated mob" end-to-end pipeline found.
- Quality loop: render a turntable PNG server-side (own software rasteriser of the cuboids) and let a vision-capable model critique; limit to 2 passes (cost).

## 4. Candidate RigSpec (JSON)
```
{ "spec":1, "id":"banshee", "archetype":"floating_ghost", "scale":1.0,
  "texture":{"size":[64,64],"palette":{"skin":"#cfd8ff","hair":"#5a6aa0","eye":"#ff3355"},
             "regions":{"head":"skin+eyes","hair":"hair","robe":"skin+gradient_fade"}},
  "bones":[{"name":"body","parent":null,"pivot":[0,12,0],"role":"torso",
            "cubes":[{"from":[-4,12,-2],"to":[4,24,2],"region":"robe","inflate":0}]},
           {"name":"head","parent":"body","role":"head","pivot":[0,24,0],"cubes":[...]},
           {"name":"arm_l","parent":"body","role":"arm_l", ...}],
  "hitbox":{"w":0.6,"h":1.9,"base_entity":"VEX|ALLAY|ZOMBIE|ARMOR_STAND_MARKER"},
  "animations":{"idle":{"clip":"float","amp":0.1,"speed":0.5,"loop":true},
                "walk":{"clip":"glide","amp":0.15},
                "attack":{"clip":"lunge","bones":["arm_l","arm_r","head"],"length":0.6},
                "hurt":{"clip":"flinch","length":0.3},
                "death":{"clip":"fade_sink","length":1.2,"loop":false}},
  "sounds":{"ambient":"sfx:wail_01","hurt":"sfx:...","death":"sfx:...","attack":"sfx:..."},
  "behavior":{"hp":30,"speed":0.25,"flying":true,"attack_dmg":4} }
```
Weapon: `{ "kind":"item", "id":"handgun", "model":{bones/cubes as above, single bone}, "display":{"firstperson_righthand":{...},"thirdperson_righthand":{...},"gui":{...},"fixed":{...}}, "states":[{"when":"use_duration|cooldown","model":"handgun_fire"}], "sounds":{"fire":..}}` -> compiled to `assets/<ns>/models/item/handgun.json` + `assets/<ns>/items/handgun.json` (+ `item_model` component set by plugin).

## 5. Validation checklist (deterministic, pre-build)
1. Schema + unknown-key rejection; bone names unique, tree acyclic, depth <= 6, bones <= 24 (display-entity cost; benchmark to confirm), cubes/bone <= 24.
2. Cube coords within -16..32 per bone model (rescale/split otherwise); rotations only single-axis 22.5 steps for vanilla item models (BetterModel's own limits UNVERIFIED).
3. Cuboid dims >= 1 px or flagged for z-fighting; zero-volume cubes rejected.
4. Texture: PNG power-of-two <= 256x256 per entity, every face has UV inside atlas, no fully transparent faces, transparent-pixel policy.
5. Animations: required idle/walk/attack/hurt/death present for mobs; lengths 0.1-10 s; keyframe times monotonic; no rotation > 360 deg per segment; death non-looping.
6. Hitbox sane vs model bounds; base entity allowed list.
7. Pack: pack_format per target version; total pack size cap (e.g. 10 MB) and sha1 stable; asset paths lowercase `[a-z0-9_/.-]`; no overwrite of vanilla namespace.
8. Round-trip test: compile spec -> .bbmodel -> load in BetterModel on a headless Paper test server, check no load errors, spawn, play each animation (CI gate, M).
9. Policy: no NSFW/copyright names/texts in generated labels; IP-sensitive skins rejected.

## 6. Vanilla-client fidelity limits
- Animation is server-driven display-entity transform interpolation: smooth but costs bandwidth per bone per viewer (UNVERIFIED magnitude); movement caps at tick rate (20 Hz) with interpolation durations; no vertex/skeletal skinning, so no bending meshes, only rigid cuboids.
- No true custom-entity hitbox shape: a vanilla base entity (invisible) provides the hit area (box/AABB only), vanilla death/hurt animations (tilt/red flash) must be suppressed; sounds via sound events in the pack.
- Item display has no collision, no shadows by default, light level fixed to its block; names/health bars via text display.
- First-person weapon: only the static item model + display transform; no real recoil animation. Fake with `select`/`range_dispatch` on use_duration/cooldown or brief model swap (works from 1.21.4; legacy CMD path on 1.21.1), muzzle flash via particles/sound.
- Pack acceptance: players get a prompt; refusing = invisible/default items. Required packs (`required` flag) can kick refusers; make this an owner setting.
- Version split: <1.21.4 uses legacy model overrides; >=1.21.4 the items/ definitions; 26.x special-type removals matter only for special models Cyrus does not use.

## 7. MVP vs later
MVP (first release):
- RigSpec schema + 3 archetypes (humanoid, quadruped, floating ghost) + prop/weapon. Size M.
- Compiler: spec -> block model JSON, items/ definition, .bbmodel, atlas PNG. M.
- Procedural animation library (5 clips). M.
- BetterModel integration: managed pre-installed plugin on Paper 1.21.4+ and 26.x; generated plugin uses compileOnly API + spawn/animate/hurt/death events. M.
- Handgun path with no engine: static item model + display transforms + sounds/particles. S.
- Resource pack merge + push (Paper `setResourcePack`, UNVERIFIED; or `server.properties` via itzg env). M.
- Validation + headless load test + turntable preview. M.
Later: flyer/serpent/spider archetypes (S each); vision critique loop (S); Texture Studio edits in-place (M); in-browser .bbmodel viewer/editor (L); IK/Molang authoring (L); 1.21.1 legacy-override pack variant (M); player-skin models/custom armor (M); BetterModel benchmark and caps (S); own minimal display-entity runtime if BetterModel becomes unmaintained (L).

## 8. Architecture recommendation
- Depend on (MIT, pre-installed, version-pinned): BetterModel. Do not depend on ModelEngine or FMM. Do not embed Blockbench.
- Build in-house: RigSpec + validator, archetype library, UV/atlas packer, procedural animation sampler, .bbmodel/Java-model emitters, pack builder/hosting, behaviour glue template (spawn, hurt/death hooks), turntable renderer. The bbmodel is a portable intermediate, so a later engine swap is cheap.
- Plugin shape: generated mod jar carries only logic + `assets/` is NOT inside the jar; Nxeon's pack service merges mod packs per server, hosts the zip, sets `resource-pack` + sha1.
- Pin: run a monthly CI that loads the golden banshee + handgun on every supported Paper version (incl. 26.x on Java 25).

## 9. Generic (non-Minecraft) rig/asset profile (5 lines)
1. Keep RigSpec engine-neutral: bones (parent, pivot, rest transform), meshes (cuboids now, triangle meshes later), materials, clips (named tracks of TRS keyframes, loop flag, events).
2. Add engine profiles that map roles and units (Minecraft pixels vs metres) and declare caps (bone/vertex/tri counts, texture sizes).
3. Exporters per target: Java model JSON, glTF 2.0 (Unity/Unreal/Godot/Hytale-style tools), bbmodel; texture to PBR channels when the profile asks for it.
4. Skinning weights + blend shapes only when a profile supports them; Minecraft profile forbids both.
5. Per-game validator plug-ins reusing the same checklist shape (budgets, naming, pack layout, licence flags).

## Sources
https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/master/README.md ; https://modrinth.com/mod/bettermodel ; https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/wiki/API-example ; https://modrinth.com/project/free-minecraft-models ; https://mythiccraft.io/index.php?resources/model-engine%E2%80%94ultimate-entity-model-manager-1-19-4-1-21-11.1213/ ; https://github.com/JannisX11/blockbench ; https://blockbench.net/wiki/docs/bbmodel ; https://minecraft.wiki/w/Items_model_definition ; https://minecraft.wiki/w/Model ; https://minecraft.wiki/w/Display ; https://github.com/jasonjgardner/blockbench-mcp-project ; BetterModel wiki index https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/wiki

| Pixelorama | MIT (VERIFIED https://github.com/Orama-Interactive/Pixelorama) | Godot app with HTML5 web export; layers with clipping masks and non-destructive effects, tilemap/seamless mode, animation timeline, palettes. Not a React component; wasm bundle is large (UNVERIFIED size). | Feature-wise the best pixel editor; iframe only. Heavy (Godot runtime), integration through file import/export only. |
| Konva | MIT, react-konva exists, active, 4,186 commits (VERIFIED https://github.com/konvajs/konva) | scene graph for custom editor; page did not mention `imageSmoothingEnabled`; one can set it on the canvas context. | Good base to BUILD our own editor in React. |
| Fabric.js, PixiJS | MIT (UNVERIFIED, memory) | Fabric = object editor, PixiJS = WebGL renderer. | Fabric not suited to pixel work; PixiJS only if we need GPU for 3D-ish later. |
| pngjs / UPNG.js / fast-png | MIT (UNVERIFIED) | PNG encode/decode; our own `lib/cyrus/textures/png.ts` already encodes. | Keep own encoder; use `pngjs` only if decode of uploads is needed. |
| skinview3d | MIT, three.js, 1.8 and HD skins, slim arms, capes (VERIFIED https://github.com/bs-community/skinview3d) | player skins only (UV fixed to the player model). Last release date not shown. | Adopt for player-skin preview; irrelevant for custom mobs. |
| deepslate | MIT, v0.27.2, WebGL structure/block rendering, loads resource packs (VERIFIED https://github.com/misode/deepslate) | summary found no entity/item model support. | Use for block preview/structures later; not for mobs. |
| minecraft-render, prismarine-viewer | UNVERIFIED (not opened) | | Not evaluated; cap hit. |

**Opinion**: no OSS editor gives layered, non-destructive, AI-candidate-aware, Minecraft-aware editing out of the box. The honest choices: (A) iframe miniPaint/Pixelorama as a quick "edit this PNG" tool, (B) build a small purpose-built pixel editor on a plain canvas or Konva (pencil, fill, line, rect, select, mirror, palette, layers, undo, tile preview). B is M-L effort but is what makes AI candidates, per-version validation and the shared studio core fit. Start with A only if time-to-market matters; replace later. Do not use Kleki branding.

## 2. Generating textures automatically

**(a) LLM-authored pixel specs rendered deterministically** (the existing `lib/cyrus/textures` DSL: palette, <=400 ops fill/px/rect/line/circle/poly/gradient/noise/shade/outline, per G-gaps).
- Strengths: free of copyright-lookalike risk from a model trained on game art (UNVERIFIED but logical), deterministic and editable (the spec IS the non-destructive source), exact palette and size, perfect alpha, trivial to keep style consistent (one shared palette per mod), cheap (a few thousand output tokens; approx. cents on Haiku/Sonnet, UNVERIFIED estimate).
- Weaknesses: organic subjects (faces, fur, glow) look blocky/amateur. Sizes above 32x32 get poor.
- Is Claude good enough? For 16x16 items, simple blocks, symbols and flat-shaded creatures: yes with a good prompt and a vision critique loop (render -> show Claude the PNG upscaled -> revise). For detailed creature skins: mediocre. I have not benchmarked this (UNVERIFIED); recommend a 30-sample eval before promising quality. Tricks: symmetry ops, a "ramp" palette (3-5 shades per material), outline-after-shade, noise-for-grain, row-string authoring for tiny sprites (16 chars per row as palette indices), and generate silhouettes first.

**(b) Image models + pixelation + quantisation.**
- FLUX: licensing page shows commercial use via tiered plans (Builder/Platform/Professional/Enterprise); output ownership text was not on the page (VERIFIED https://bfl.ai/licensing). Models named: FLUX.2 [klein] Base 9B and [dev] sit behind paid tiers. Self-hosting needs a GPU.
- Retro Diffusion (Astropulse): pixel-art-specific models, "Minecraft items/textures", sprites, tilesets, 90+ styles, API and MCP server; used by Replicate, Poe, Scenario (search snippet, UNVERIFIED https://mcpservers.org/servers/retro-diffusion/retro-diffusion-mcp; direct fetch returned 403). Commercial terms are in its ToS (not read) and price per image not found. Strongest pixel-art candidate; check seamless tiling and transparency options before use.
- Generic pipeline: generate at 512-1024, downscale with nearest/box to 16/32/64, quantise to a fixed palette (median-cut or an owner-chosen mod palette), clean alpha with threshold/flood fill. Without a pixel-tuned model, results look like blurry downscaled images with dithering noise. Seamless tiling: generate with tileable flag if offered or enforce by offset-and-inpaint (hard). Style consistency across a mod: reuse seed/palette/style reference; hardest for (b).
- Copyright risk: image models can reproduce vanilla Minecraft look or other IP; a vanilla-lookalike policy check (reject prompts naming Mojang/other games' IP, perceptual-hash against vanilla textures) is advisable (UNVERIFIED approach). Mojang's usage rules for assets are separate (not researched).
- Hosted vendor terms and cost: not determined; third-party name must not appear to customers (brand rule).

**(c) Hybrid (recommended)**: Claude plans an asset sheet (palette, silhouette, materials) -> produce candidate A from the DSL; optionally candidate B from a pixel model; both snapped to the mod palette; Claude vision picks/flags; user sees both as candidates. Raise (b) later; keep (a) as the default free path. Cost per texture: (a) cents, (b) UNVERIFIED cents to tens of cents.

**Entity skins/UV**: A custom mob on a vanilla base entity (zombie) uses that entity's fixed UV layout (e.g. `textures/entity/...`), so the studio needs a per-base-model UV template and region overlay. The player layout is 64x64 with an outer overlay layer, slim arm = 3px, inner layer must be opaque on Java (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Skin). Fully custom models (Blockbench-style JSON via item/display-entity tricks) need their own UVs: that is a model-pipeline question outside this file (see mob-model research, if any).

## 3. Validation checklist (per version)

- PNG only; item/block textures may be non-square since 1.13 but stretch on default models (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Resource_pack). Keep square, power-of-two (16/32/64/128) by default (UNVERIFIED best practice).
- Paths: `assets/<ns>/textures/{item,block,entity}/...` (VERIFIED same page); lowercase `[a-z0-9_/.-]`, no spaces (UNVERIFIED but standard).
- Animation: sidecar `<name>.png.mcmeta` with `animation:{frames, frametime(default 1 tick), interpolate(default false), width, height}`; the PNG is a strip of frames; frame size must divide image (VERIFIED same page for fields; divisibility check UNVERIFIED).
- Pack format: 1.21 line 34-53 through 1.21.5; 26.1 = 76-84; 26.2 = 85-88; 26.3 = 89-97; 26.4 (upcoming) = 98-100 (VERIFIED same page); `min_format`/`max_format` supported in pack.mcmeta; 26.1 resource pack format 84.0 (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_26.1). Existing `packFormatFor` returns 75 for 26.x, which is wrong; flag stale (this wiki data is current only as of fetch date).
- 1.21.4+ item models go through `assets/<ns>/items/<id>.json` plus `models/item` (existing pack.ts does this per G-gaps); 26.1 block-model textures can be objects with `sprite` and `force_translucent` (VERIFIED 26.1 page).
- Emissive/overlay conventions (e.g. `_e` emissive suffix, `_overlay`): these are mostly OptiFine/CIT/Iris-style or entity-specific (eyes layers for spiders/endermen) conventions, NOT vanilla for custom textures - UNVERIFIED, do not promise emissive glow in vanilla.
- Alpha: skin inner layer opaque (Java); cutout vs translucent behavior depends on the model/block render type (26.1 `force_translucent`).
- Pack size: warn if > ~50 MB (UNVERIFIED client-prompt behaviour).

## 4. Editing UX for opening a mod's textures

- Source of truth = `TextureSpec` (DSL) plus optional raster layers; PNG is a build artifact. Open asset -> editor loads spec -> user edits in raster layers placed above the generated base layer ("generated" layer locked/regenerable; "paint" layers editable).
- AI edit = a **candidate**: model returns a new spec or PNG; shown side-by-side/onion-skinned; user accepts into a new layer or discards. Never overwrite silently; every accepted change is one undo step with provenance row.
- Version history per asset (content-hash) so "revert to generated" works. Live preview: 16x tile preview (tiling), item preview in inventory slot size, 3D preview via skinview3d (player skins) or three.js for simple cube blocks (deepslate for structures).
- Ledger: same provenance model as Sound (D-sound.md): source = dsl/ai-model/upload, licence, hash.

## 5. Shared studio core with per-game profiles (survey)

Core (game-agnostic): asset registry + versioning, layer stack with non-destructive recipes, undo history, candidate/AI-suggestion workflow, provenance ledger, preview host, export pipeline interface (`validate`, `render`, `package`), plan gating hooks. Both studios (sound recipes, texture layers) share these.
**Pixel profile (Minecraft)**: fixed sizes (16/32/64), nearest-neighbour, palette-first, index/colour limits, tile preview, per-asset UV templates, .mcmeta animation editor, pack-format validator, 16-colour-ramp helpers.
**Realistic/PBR/3D profile (later)**: multi-channel maps (albedo, normal, roughness/metallic, AO, emissive), 2K-4K sizes, GPU-based viewport (three.js/PixiJS), mesh + UV unwrap import (glTF/FBX), engine-specific exporters (Unreal/Unity/Source/Rust-style bundle formats), seamless-tiling synthesis and AI texture models (different tools: diffusion + height-to-normal). Mostly separate editor features, so keep the core small and let profiles plug in tools and validators. UNVERIFIED survey from knowledge; no sources opened for PBR.

## 6. MVP vs later (S <= 2 days, M ~ 1 wk, L multi-week)

MVP: wire existing `textures/` to the build (items) and extend `pack.ts` for blocks/entities/mcmeta + corrected `packFormatFor` (M); Claude spec generation + render + vision critique loop (M); validator (S-M); studio v1 = purpose-built pixel editor (pencil/fill/line/rect/select/mirror/layers/undo/palette/tile preview) (L), or iframe miniPaint stopgap (S-M); candidate workflow + ledger (M); skinview3d preview (S). Later: pixel image model path (M-L), UV templates for vanilla base mobs (M each), animation editor (M), PBR profile (L+).
Build: DSL, validators, editor, candidate workflow. Adopt: miniPaint (stopgap), skinview3d, three.js. Avoid: Kleki branding; Piskel as embed; any generator whose terms were not read.

Risks: model art lookalikes; vendor ToS unread; editor scope creep; wiki pack-format tables change monthly. Could not determine: Claude's actual pixel quality (needs eval), image-API prices, minecraft-render/prismarine status, exact LICENSE files, last-release dates for several repos.

# D - Sound Studio research (step 5), 2026-10-10

Labels: VERIFIED (url) = I opened it this session. UNVERIFIED = memory or search snippet only. Page budget used: 12 of 12 (some fetches returned thin summaries, noted).

## 1. Minecraft Java sound system

**sounds.json** (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sounds.json)
- Lives at `assets/<namespace>/sounds.json` in a resource pack. Top level maps an **event key** (e.g. `entity.zombie.hurt`, or a custom `banshee.wail`) to `{ "replace": bool, "subtitle": "<lang key>", "sounds": [...] }`.
- Each `sounds` entry is either a bare string (file path without `.ogg`, optional `namespace:` prefix) or an object: `name`, `type` (`file` default, or `event` to reference another event), `volume` (>0, default 1), `pitch` (>0, default 1), `weight` (int, random pick bias), `stream` (true for long sounds; wiki recommends it for music/records), `attenuation_distance` (int), `preload` (bool).
- Event vs file: the game plays an **event key**; the engine picks one entry from the list by weight (variants). Files are the raw Ogg Vorbis. Variants are how you avoid repetition (author 3-4 per hurt/step).
- `replace: true` discards the vanilla list for that event; false/absent appends to vanilla variants.
- Format: **Ogg Vorbis required**. **Mono = positional** (volume falls with distance); **stereo = constant volume** regardless of distance. So every mob/world sound must be mono; only music/UI may be stereo. All VERIFIED same URL.
- Custom namespaces: use `namespace:key` / `namespace:path` (VERIFIED same URL). Put a plugin's keys in its own namespace (e.g. `nxeon_banshee:`), never `minecraft:`.
- Subtitles: `subtitle` is a translation key; the text must exist in `assets/<ns>/lang/en_us.json` (UNVERIFIED detail, standard behaviour).

**What a pack can override vs add** (reasoning; UNVERIFIED in game by me)
- Override `entity.<mob>.hurt/death/ambient/step`: changes that sound for EVERY vanilla mob of that type server-wide, for each player with the pack. Fine for a total-conversion, bad for a mod that adds one "banshee" built on a zombie.
- Add new keys (`ns:banshee.wail`): triggered only by plugin code. This is the right default for Cyrus: new keys, plugin plays them, and silences the vanilla base mob (`Entity#setSilent(true)`, UNVERIFIED API name) so vanilla zombie groans do not overlap.
- Plugin playback (Paper/Bukkit): `World#playSound(Location, String key, SoundCategory, volume, pitch)` and `Player#playSound(...)` take a **string key**, so custom keys work without an enum (UNVERIFIED signatures; check against the Paper jar's javap during build sheets). Category (`HOSTILE`, `NEUTRAL`, `PLAYERS`, `AMBIENT`, `MASTER`...) controls the client's per-category volume slider. Volume above 1.0 extends audible range (rule of thumb ~16 blocks x volume; UNVERIFIED).
- If the player lacks the pack, an unknown key plays silently, so a mod must degrade gracefully.

**Versions**: wiki's sounds.json page has no 1.21.x/26.x entries (VERIFIED same URL), i.e. the schema looks stable since 1.13 (`preload`). 26.1 is the first year-based release; resource pack format is now **84.0** (VERIFIED https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_26.1), which matches G-gaps: pack.ts tables are wrong for 26.x. 26.1 also added baby-mob and adult-variant sounds (same URL), so vanilla event names have grown; do not hard-code a list, read keys from the version's asset index. Pack metadata (`pack.mcmeta`, min/max format) is a pack-builder concern, not a sounds.json one. 1.21.11 -> 26.x pack_format deltas for sounds: none found.

**Complete mob sound set** (durations/levels are conventions, UNVERIFIED; tune against vanilla files by measuring them with ffprobe/ebur128 during MVP):

| event | purpose | variants | length | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ambient/idle | random loop-free grunt | 3 | 0.8-2.5 s | quietest, low pitch jitter |
| hurt | damage taken | 3 | 0.2-0.6 s | sharp transient |
| death | on death | 1-2 | 0.6-1.8 s | longest decay |
| step | per footstep | 4 | 0.08-0.25 s | very short, no tail |
| attack | melee swing/bite | 2-3 | 0.3-0.8 s | loud transient |
| special | ability/charge/roar/boss phase | 1-2 each | 0.5-3 s | one key per ability |
| spawn | summon/appear | 1 | 0.8-2.5 s | optional |

Loudness: peak-normalise to about -3 dBFS, attack/death loudest, step/ambient 6-10 dB lower; use `volume` in sounds.json for relative balance rather than re-baking (UNVERIFIED convention). Mono, 44.1 kHz, trimmed with 5 ms fades to avoid clicks. Keep files small (pack size matters for the join prompt).

## 2. Ogg Vorbis pipeline

- **Server-side ffmpeg + libvorbis (recommended).** FFmpeg is LGPL 2.1 by default and becomes GPL 2 if GPL parts are enabled (`--enable-gpl`) (VERIFIED https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html). That page does NOT address libvorbis or the separate-process case (it said so). libvorbis/libogg are BSD-3 (VERIFIED https://github.com/erikh2000/sl-web-ogg, bundled Xiph COPYING files). Calling ffmpeg as a subprocess on a service we run, never redistributing the binary, is the low-risk pattern; legal sign-off still advisable (UNVERIFIED legal reading). Distro ffmpeg is often built with GPL flags; use the distro package unmodified on the server (no redistribution) or a static LGPL build.
- Command shape: `ffmpeg -nostdin -i in.wav -ac 1 -ar 44100 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 out.ogg` (UNVERIFIED flags; the native `vorbis` encoder is experimental, prefer libvorbis).
- **Safe use on the build host**: spawn with an argv array (no shell), `-protocol_whitelist file` and file inputs only (no URLs), CPU/time/memory limits (`timeout`, cgroup), max input size and duration (e.g. 60 s), run in the existing build container, never feed user-supplied filter strings. ffmpeg decoders have a CVE history, so keep it patched and sandboxed.
- `oggenc` (vorbis-tools) is GPL-2 (UNVERIFIED); fine as a separate process but ffmpeg already covers it and decodes MP3, so skip it.
- **Browser/wasm**: `sl-web-ogg` MIT + BSD-3 Xiph parts, `encodeAudioBuffer()` with quality param, promise API, only 17 commits and 0 stars (VERIFIED https://github.com/erikh2000/sl-web-ogg) - immature, treat as a fallback. `libvorbis.js` (itsjoesullivan) BSD-style but old (UNVERIFIED, search snippet). `@wasm-audio-decoders/ogg-vorbis` is decode only (snippet). Browser audio element can already decode Vorbis for preview.
- **Recommendation**: the browser works in WAV/Float32 (`AudioBuffer`) and uploads WAV (or a small JSON edit recipe); the server renders and encodes. This keeps one deterministic encoder, one licence story and lets AI/automatic sound design (no browser) use the same path. Effort S-M.

## 3. Editing UI libraries

| lib | licence | fit |
|---|---|---|
| wavesurfer.js | BSD-3-Clause; v8; plugins Regions, Timeline, Minimap, Envelope, Spectrogram (VERIFIED https://github.com/katspaugh/wavesurfer.js) | waveform display + trim regions + fade envelope UI. Its own docs say it does not process audio. Use as the **view**. |
| Tone.js | MIT, active, `Tone.Offline`, Reverb, Filter, FeedbackDelay, Distortion, pitch shifting (VERIFIED https://github.com/Tonejs/Tone.js) | good for offline rendering of a graph in the browser; heavy (~hundreds KB); optional. |
| howler.js | MIT, 25k stars, playback only (VERIFIED https://github.com/goldfire/howler.js) | not needed; Web Audio suffices. |
| Web Audio (`OfflineAudioContext`) | browser standard | gain, fade (gain ramps), `playbackRate` pitch+speed, `BiquadFilter`, `Convolver` reverb, `DynamicsCompressor`; enough for MVP with no library. |
| audiobuffer-to-wav, jsfx | UNVERIFIED (small MIT-ish utilities) | WAV writer is ~40 lines; write our own. |

Pitch without speed change needs a phase vocoder; skip in MVP (resample pitch only, which is what Minecraft's own `pitch` does).

**Non-destructive recipe** (stored as JSON, source files immutable):
```
{ sourceId, trim:{start,end}, fadeIn, fadeOut, gainDb, pitchSemitones,
  eq:[{type,freq,gain,q}], reverb:{irId,mix}, normalizePeakDb }
```
Layers each carry a recipe, a start offset and a gain; render = sum, then limiter, then mono downmix, then Vorbis. The browser previews via `OfflineAudioContext`; the server re-renders the same recipe for the shipped file. Caveat: browser and server renders must match, so the server is authoritative and the UI preview is approximate. Keep recipe version numbers.

## 4. Automatic sound design

**(a) Procedural synthesis presets** (extend `lib/cyrus/sfx.ts`, which today is UI-only per G-gaps): per sound class a deterministic generator seeded from the spec: growl (saw + formant filters + noise), wail (FM sine glide + vibrato + reverb), hit (noise burst + low sine thump), step (filtered noise click), zap, magic chime. Cheap, free, original, no provenance risk, but sounds synthetic. Effort M. Run it in Node via an offline renderer (the code uses Web Audio; port to a pure-DSP render function; UNVERIFIED how sfx.ts is structured).

**(b) Layering from the owner's 514 SFX library**: filename-prefix tags (Whoosh/Hit/Explosion/Door/Alert...) become a tag index; the LLM picks 1-3 layers per event by tag plus pitch/gain/filters (e.g. low-pass + -7 semitones on an Explosion for a death boom). Pitch-shifting, layering and filtering turns 514 into thousands of distinct sounds. It is the best quality/cost path. Needs the library on the build host, a tag index (can be generated from filenames), and the owner's customer licence. Layer-per-event limit and a "no raw unchanged file" rule are optional policy. Effort M.

**(c) AI generation**:
- Stable Audio Open 1.0: open weights, up to 47 s stereo 44.1 kHz, trained on Freesound CC0/CC-BY/CC-Sampling+ and FMA, "better for sound effects than music", needs a CUDA GPU (VERIFIED https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-1.0). Licence: Stability Community License - free commercial use under USD 1M annual revenue, **registration required**, no using outputs to train foundation models, "Powered by Stability AI" attribution where distributed (VERIFIED https://stability.ai/community-license-agreement). Needs a GPU box Nxeon may not have; no cost per call otherwise. Risky for attribution and registration.
- ElevenLabs Sound Effects API: 0.1-30 s, loopable, MP3 or 48 kHz WAV (non-looping), 40 credits/s when duration specified (VERIFIED https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/sound-effects). Commercial use only on paid plans, no competing-product use (UNVERIFIED, from third-party search snippets; read the actual terms before use). Hosted, sub-minute latency (UNVERIFIED), per-second cost, and it adds a third-party dependency (brand rule: never name it to customers).
- AudioLDM-class (AudioLDM2 weights are non-commercial CC BY-NC as I recall, UNVERIFIED) - avoid unless checked. Not opened due to the page cap; AudioGen/AudioCraft are CC-BY-NC for weights (UNVERIFIED), also avoid.
- Judgment: AI output is useful for textures-of-sound (creature vocals, ambient beds) where layering the owner library falls short; make it a **later** add-on behind a provider interface, every output entering the ledger.

## 5. SoundSpec proposal

```
SoundSpec { version, profile:"minecraft-java", namespace,
  events:[{ key:"banshee.wail", category:"hostile",
     role:"ambient"|"hurt"|"death"|"step"|"attack"|"special"|"spawn",
     variants:[{ weight, volume, pitch, layers:[Layer], mono:true, lengthMs, tailMs }],
     subtitle, stream:false, attenuationDistance }] }
Layer { source:{kind:"library"|"synth"|"ai"|"upload", id|preset|prompt|provenanceId},
        offsetMs, gainDb, recipe:EditRecipe }
```
The compiler turns this into `sounds.json` + Ogg files + lang subtitles + a plugin event table (`role`->key), so Java code never contains file paths. LLM output is schema-validated (event count, length, tag ids must exist, no 'minecraft:' keys unless override is chosen).

**Provenance/licence ledger** (row per layer per render): `{ assetId, kind, licence ("owner-original"|"cc0"|"cc-by"|"generated-<provider>"|"user-upload"), sourceRef (library filename+hash / model+version+prompt hash / upload hash), attributionRequired, commercialOk, customerLicenceVersion, recipeHash, outputHash, userId, createdAt }`. Gate: NxLabs publication refuses public pages when any layer is user-upload without attestation or `attributionRequired` unmet (hook into `public-gate.ts`, per G-gaps). Owner library rows are marked with the licence version once the owner writes it.

## 6. MVP vs later (S <= 2 days, M ~ 1 wk, L multi-week)

MVP: SoundSpec + compiler (sounds.json, lang, ffmpeg encode, pack integration) M; library tag index + LLM layer picking + render service (server DSP: trim/fade/gain/pitch/lowpass/layer) M-L; gate/ledger table S-M; Studio UI with wavesurfer.js (Regions/Envelope) + OfflineAudioContext preview + variant list M; plugin glue (`playSound` helper, silence base mob) S. Later: synthesis presets M, reverb IRs S, pitch-preserving stretch M, AI provider interface L, community sound sharing L.
Build: SoundSpec, compiler, recipe renderer, ledger. Adopt: ffmpeg/libvorbis, wavesurfer.js, Web Audio. Avoid: howler (not needed), NC-licensed models, sl-web-ogg as primary encoder.

Risks: GPL ffmpeg build if redistributed; browser/server render mismatch; customer ownership terms for the owner's library not yet written; vanilla event names change per version.
Could not determine: mob sound lengths from real vanilla files, exact Paper `playSound` overloads on 26.x, ElevenLabs/Stability output terms beyond snippets, quality of any AI model by listening.
# F: Quality + market research (step 7), 2026-10-10

Pages opened: 15 of 16 cap. Labels: VERIFIED (url) = opened; UNVERIFIED = memory/inference or search snippet only. Internal facts come from BRIEF.md/G-gaps.md (owner-verified).

## 1. Competitor landscape (AI game-mod creation)

Best single source: Player Games' own comparison page (VERIFIED https://www.player.games/de-DE/best-ai-minecraft-mod-maker, "last verified 2026-07-15"). It is vendor-authored, so treat rankings as marketing; the facts about rivals are still useful.

Plugins "finish in a few minutes, complex within 30" | Full source delivered; boot-validation as a headline feature; multi-loader; Hytale | No Forge; no bundled server; daily credit limits; version support not stated on plugin page |
